priors.applicability: Prefer when the bowl pose is reliable and displaced relative to the demonstrations, while the container is securely held and the observed container-to-TCP grasp is near the nominal support. It is also the default for a nominal complete carry-pour-right trajectory because it preserves absolute bowl clearance. The high-level agent should not invoke any pour policy for an open or uncertain grasp or a source below safe clearance.

handoff.entry_conditions: The source is visibly closed in the gripper and lifted clear of support, from the early-lift states represented at action 180 through the staged bowl-centered states near actions 320-360. Bowl pose must be observed and the target must be reachable from the measured Panda configuration.
handoff.exit_conditions: At least ten particles are observed settled within the bowl, the source is approximately upright and still held, and outbound motion toward the return region has started. Nominal takeover support spans actions 1460-1740, with near-upright states around 1680.
handoff.failure_signatures: Open or widening fingers, loss of the rigid source-to-TCP relationship, source below bowl-wall clearance, source or TCP target outside IK reach, particles outside the bowl, particles still in the source when righting begins, or an IK non-convergence diagnostic. Demonstrations do not establish recovery from spills, slips or collisions.
handoff.overlap_role: Every binding retains action supervision [180,360) shared with grasp_lift_stage and [1460,1740) shared with return_place_release. The first overlap teaches lift/carry continuation; the second teaches late righting and outbound transport.
handoff.successor_readiness: return_place_release is ready after observed transfer completion and near-upright source orientation, nominally around action 1680; the 280-step outgoing overlap supports earlier takeover during righting and later takeover during outbound travel.

priors.invocation_contract: {"call_args_schema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{},"required":[]},"parameter_semantics":"No caller parameters. The executor supplies two causal observed states. The policy resolves the current world bowl pose from each state and decodes each learned bowl-frame TCP target through the fresh observed bowl pose and measured Panda joints."}
priors.limitations: Bowl displacement invariance is structural for the TCP carry, pour and righting arc, but reachability, bowl-wall clearance and the independently fixed return target remain physical dependencies. The demonstrations keep the bowl fixed, so improved behavior under bowl displacement is an expected benefit, not observed evidence. Direct TCP targets do not compensate for a substantially different or slipping grasp; prefer the source-motion prior then. Particle outcomes in the demonstrations are nominal and do not prove recovery.
priors.pipeline_implications: This is the displacement specialist and nominal default. Route reliable bowl displacement here. If the state is phase-ambiguous because discharge is early, late or partial, route to the particle-set residual prior. If a secure but unusual container-to-TCP transform is observed, route to the source-motion prior. Terminate only from the unchanged task evidence, not from elapsed time alone.
priors.rationale: All inspected demonstrations first move the held source from variable early lift states near the pickup area to a high source pose around (-0.259, 0.224, 0.400) m over the bowl, then execute a tilt/right arc while remaining bowl-centered. The bowl itself is fixed in training, so a world-target policy can confound the demonstrated coordinates with the relationship. Learning commanded TCP poses as SE(3) targets in the observed bowl frame makes the carry, pour and righting geometry equivariant to bowl translation and rotation by construction. Inputs retain measured qpos/qvel and relative source, particle and return-target context, because task-space invariance does not remove reachability, grasp or outbound-goal dependencies. The unchanged standard diffusion backbone is sufficient.
priors.statement: Bowl-frame absolute TCP trajectory prior: diffuse each commanded Cartesian TCP target as bowl-relative position, continuous 6D orientation and gripper command, then compose it with the freshly observed bowl pose and solve IK from freshly measured joints.

priors.applicability: Prefer for a securely held source when the current intermediate state is uncertain in phase: particles may have discharged earlier or later than nominal, the policy is entered mid-tilt or mid-righting, or a small execution deviation should be corrected from the fresh TCP. Reliable particle, bowl, container and TCP observations are required. Do not use particle motion alone as proof of contact or grasp.

handoff.entry_conditions: The source is securely closed in the gripper and clear of support. Entry may be in early carry, at the staged pose, during the tilt/discharge arc, or during righting if the observed relational state remains within demonstrated nominal phases and the next local motion is reachable.
handoff.exit_conditions: Observed particle geometry indicates at least ten particles settled in the bowl; the source is approximately upright, remains held, and is beginning outbound motion. The unchanged success and successor conditions are not replaced by the learned phase auxiliary.
handoff.failure_signatures: Uncertain/open grasp, large relocation beyond local residual support, particle observations that are missing or implausible, particles outside bowl bounds, collision or spill, non-converged IK, or oscillation between tilt and righting. Successful nominal data do not establish recovery from these failures.
handoff.overlap_role: All [180,360) incoming and [1460,1740) outgoing actions remain supervised. This permits the phase-aware model to continue from grasp_lift_stage and to overlap return_place_release throughout late righting and early outbound carry.
handoff.successor_readiness: Hand off to return_place_release only when observed particle settlement and source uprightness support it. Nominal readiness is near 1680, with supervised flexibility across 1460-1740.

priors.invocation_contract: {"call_args_schema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{},"required":[]},"parameter_semantics":"No caller parameters. The executor supplies two causal states. Particle tokens are built only from current/past observations; each learned action is a local SE(3) displacement from the TCP observed immediately before that demonstrated action and is applied from the fresh TCP at execution."}
priors.limitations: The local residual representation is not structurally anchored to a far-away bowl, so large bowl relocations or long open-loop errors should use the bowl-frame prior. The set encoder can distinguish observed geometric phases but cannot infer hidden contact truth or guarantee that a particle is inside the source under severe occlusion/noise. The auxiliary current-phase labels regularize representation learning; they do not change success or authorize early handoff. Demonstrations contain no spill or slip recovery.
priors.pipeline_implications: Use this as the phase/intermediate-state specialist. Its fresh-TCP residual decoder should reduce sensitivity to small state deviations, while the pooled particle encoder and phase auxiliary expose discharge progress without particle identity. Route major bowl displacement to the bowl-frame prior and route an unusual rigid grasp transform to the source-motion prior.
priors.rationale: The demonstrated discharge timing varies despite similar arm motion. In demo12300 at 800 several particles are still airborne or near the source while some are settled; in demo12303 at 800 all twelve are already on the bowl floor. By 900-1100 both runs show settled particles while the arm reaches and leaves maximum tilt. A flat identity-sensitive particle vector and world action can make tilt/right phase ambiguous. A shared per-particle encoder with symmetric mean/max pooling is invariant to particle ordering, and explicit bowl-relative and source-relative particle geometry exposes settlement and remaining-source evidence. A small auxiliary head predicts current settled fraction, source fraction and source uprightness from the same causal condition, with a masked MSE gradient through the set encoder. Local TCP-frame translation and rotation-vector actions are decoded from each fresh measured TCP, targeting small execution deviations. The standard diffusion U-Net remains unchanged after the condition encoder.
priors.statement: Permutation-invariant particle-phase prior with fresh-TCP residual actions: encode unordered relational particle tokens and causal robot/source context, regularize the shared condition with current phase labels, and diffuse local TCP-frame SE(3) displacements plus the gripper command.

priors.applicability: Prefer when the source remains securely and rigidly held but the observed container-to-TCP transform is unusual relative to nominal demonstrations, or the predecessor delivers a modestly displaced source/TCP entry state. Container, TCP and bowl poses must be reliable and the resulting source motion must remain reachable. Never use this compensation as evidence that a grasp exists.

handoff.entry_conditions: The source is closed in the gripper, visibly lifted and moving rigidly with the TCP. Entry can occur throughout the supervised [180,360) lift/carry overlap, including the observed start-height range, or at a later nominal pour/right state if the rigid transform is still trustworthy.
handoff.exit_conditions: Particles are observed settled to the unchanged threshold, the source itself—not just the TCP—is approximately upright, the grasp remains rigid, and outbound motion is under way within the [1460,1740) overlap.
handoff.failure_signatures: An open or slipping grasp, rapid change in the measured container-to-TCP transform, pose-estimation noise that creates implausible compensation, unreachable compensated TCP pose, bowl collision, spill, remaining particles during righting, or IK non-convergence. No demonstrated recovery supports continuing after these signatures.
handoff.overlap_role: The complete [180,360) and [1460,1740) action intervals are supervised. Object-motion labels are derived without trimming those intervals, so grasp_lift_stage and return_place_release retain substantial shared commands despite the changed Cartesian representation.
handoff.successor_readiness: return_place_release can take over after particle settlement and near-upright source orientation, nominally near 1680; keep this policy active longer only when its rigid-grasp compensation remains needed during outbound motion.

priors.invocation_contract: {"call_args_schema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{},"required":[]},"parameter_semantics":"No caller parameters. The executor supplies two causal observations. The learned action is a desired source-container SE(3) increment in the current observed container frame. Decoding composes that increment with the fresh container pose and fresh observed rigid container-to-TCP transform, then solves IK from fresh measured joints."}
priors.limitations: Compensation assumes the observed source-to-TCP transform is rigid over the action and cannot recover a lost or sliding grasp. Source-local increments are robust to modest displaced entries but are not an absolute destination anchor; use the bowl-frame prior for large bowl displacement. Particle timing ambiguity is handled more explicitly by the particle-set prior. The training grasp transforms are nominal and vary only modestly, so benefit for unusual secure grasps is expected rather than demonstrated.
priors.pipeline_implications: Use this as the grasp-geometry and displaced-entry specialist when a rigid but atypical source-to-TCP relation is observed. Its source-level motion preserves the intended container attitude and lip trajectory better than replaying a nominal TCP path. Route substantial destination displacement to the bowl-frame prior and partial-discharge/phase ambiguity to the particle-set residual prior. Abort rather than compensate when rigidity is doubtful.
priors.rationale: Pour success depends on source pose, not TCP pose alone. The observations provide both container and TCP poses, and the demonstrated gripper stays closed throughout all inspected entry, pour, righting and outbound points. For each label, the demonstrated commanded TCP pose and the observed rigid container-to-TCP transform define a desired source pose. Diffusing the desired source increment in the current container frame removes global source displacement from the learned action and, during decoding, reattaches that source motion through the freshly observed grasp transform. Thus an off-center but rigid grasp changes the required TCP target by construction. Measured qpos/qvel and source/bowl/target relations remain in the causal input because source invariance does not remove IK reachability or destination geometry. This uses the unchanged standard backbone and a representation distinct from both bowl-absolute TCP targets and current-TCP rotation-vector residuals.
priors.statement: Rigid-grasp source-motion prior: diffuse desired container-frame source increments with 6D orientation, reconstruct the corresponding world TCP target using the fresh observed source-to-TCP transform, and solve IK from measured joints.
